statement: To test that a batched or paged read keeps its outputs in order, without a test hook in the code, use a consumer that stops at its first match. Place two matches in different batches, and assert which one the result cites. Cejel #586: a mutant that collected A2's batched history outputs in reverse survived every fixture. Findings were compared as sets, and a check of each batch's input order cannot see the output side. The history secret scan stops at the first secret in entry order and cites that commit. A fixture with one secret in the newest batch and one in the oldest therefore cites the newer commit, and reversed, unshifted or dropped outputs make it cite the older one, or nothing. Rules: find a short-circuiting consumer downstream of the read; put the expected match first and a decoy last; also put a sole finding in the first batch, so a dropped first output is caught.
